$comment: Generated from CHANGELOG.md by scripts/releases.mjs — don't edit. Apps' jimbo-ui config section reads it to show what a newer release changes.

releases.summary: Symmetry, scrollbars that always show, and job tiles that put progress first; changes that load look like they're loading, and can be cancelled.

items.text: `Page` in the kit: every page's frame. `AppShell`'s main is now a column at least the screen's height, and a `Page` takes all of it, so a page low on content fills the screen: its `Section fill` or `EmptyState fill` (new) stretches down to the dock. Guide section 6: pages fill the screen.
Cards side by side are one size: `MediaGrid`, `List layout="tiles"` and `StatGrid` make every row as tall as the tallest card, and each card fills its cell. Guide section 6.

`Columns` in the kit: sections or cards side by side (`count` 2 or 3, from `lg:` or `sm:`), every row one height. Guide section 6 makes symmetry a rule: nothing in a row is shorter than its neighbour.

Scrollbars always show. `globals.css` themes every scrollbar inside the page — a `surface-2` lane with a `text-subtle` thumb (≥ 3:1 on the lane in every look and tone), `text-muted` on hover, accent while dragged — and in Chrome and Safari it stays visible on macOS too, so a capped list plainly scrolls. New utilities `.scroll-area` and `.scroll-area-x`; `List maxHeight` caps a list of rows and scrolls inside its card. Guide sections 6 and 7; never hide a scrollbar (section 12).

`JobTile` (`ui/feedback.tsx`): one job in a "running now" list, made for `List layout="tiles"`. A large percentage with the count beside it and a thick bar first, the item it's on in readable type on an accent wash, then a note and a compact block of facts (speed, time left, updated) at the bottom; `done`, `failed` and `queued` are compact (name, badge, note). Text wraps instead of being cut. `ProgressBar size="lg"` is its thick bar.
Guide section 6: an item's page is a path — the singular kind and its name (`/service/mail`), never `?id=` or the list's path with the item after it.

`Pending` in the kit: wraps a result that's being replaced after a control changed. The old result stays, dimmed, under a glass bar ("Sorting…") after 150 ms, with Cancel after a second. `useSettled` remembers the last view whose data arrived, so Cancel can abort the request and put the control back. Guide section 7 makes it the rule: nothing looks like it did nothing.
`Section`'s card stretches to fill its cell, content at the top, so two sections side by side in a grid are one height (one with a line under its chart no longer leaves its neighbour short).
`PillTabs scroll` shows its scrollbar under the row instead of hiding it, and a `Sheet`'s body keeps its bar showing.
The Dashboard and Status archetypes put their charts in `Columns`; the Dashboard adds a "Running now" list of `JobTile`s.

`setUrlParams` (`lib/useUrlState.ts`) started from React Router 6's updater argument, which holds the params from the last render, so two sets in one handler (a sort, then its page back to 1) dropped the first. It now starts from the live URL. **Apps must:** Nothing — copy the foundation files (`styles/globals.css` brings the scrollbars and `.scroll-area`) and `lib/useUrlState.ts` again. Available to adopt from `reference/`: `Pending`, `Page` and the `fill` props (port `AppShell`'s main, a `flex flex-1 flex-col` column, and wrap pages in `Page` to have short pages fill the screen); `Section`'s stretching card and `Columns` (replace `grid lg:grid-cols-2` around sections with `Columns`); `List maxHeight` in place of a hand-capped `overflow-y-auto` list; `PillTabs`' visible bar (drop `[scrollbar-width:none]` and the hidden webkit bar from any copy); `JobTile` and `ProgressBar size` from `ui/feedback.tsx` for a running-now list. An app that hid a scrollbar itself can drop that to match. **Available:** `Columns`, `JobTile`, `.scroll-area`, `.scroll-area-x`, `List maxHeight`, `ProgressBar size`, `Pending`, `useSettled`, `Page`.

releases.summary: Card grids in three sizes, bar-chart columns that link, and text that never overflows.

items.text: `MediaGrid` in the kit: the grid for `MediaCard`s, with `size` — `sm` (three across on phones, four, five, then six wide; cards take smaller type and padding), `md` (two, three, four; the default, as the hand-written grids were) or `lg` (one, two, three). Cards read the size from the grid, so `MediaCard` has no new prop.

Vertical `BarChart` columns with a `to` link: a click or Enter goes there; on touch the first tap reads the value and a second tap on the same column goes; the readout above gets an *Open* link either way. Horizontal rows already linked.
The Style guide shows a small `MediaGrid` and linked vertical bars.

**New rule: text never overflows, it's trimmed** (guide section 6, SKILL core rules). Every kit text slot now cuts with an ellipsis: `KeyValue` label and value on one line (a value never wraps mid-value, and takes up to 65% of the row); stacked values clamp at three lines; `Section` titles, `StatTile` labels and values, `SwitchRow` labels, `Badge`, `LinkChips` labels, `RangeField` labels, `BarChart`'s readout and `EntityRow` meta (capped at 40%) truncate; `PageHeader` and `Sheet` titles clamp at two lines, `HeroSection` and `Hero` titles and hero text at three, `StatTile` sub lines and `SwitchRow` hints at two. `StatTile` values use `leading-tight` so a truncated number keeps its descenders. **Available:** `MediaGrid`, `MediaSize`. **Apps must:** Nothing — copy the foundation files. Port the kit when you want the new pieces and the trimming, and trim text the same way in the app's own components.

releases.summary: App-wide search: the ⌘K palette becomes Spotlight for the app, and no zoom in the installed app.

items.text: **App-wide search (Spotlight)** in `components/ui/overlays.tsx`. `CommandPalette` takes the app's search `providers` (`SearchProvider`: `id`, `label`, `search(query, signal)`, `pick`, optional `preview`, `more`, `limit`, `debounce`): results come live, debounced and cancelled when the query moves on, grouped by provider with a loading row, an error line and an empty state. Rows have an optional 40 px thumbnail (an image, or the theme's motif for `image: null`), title, subtitle and meta. A preview pane shows the highlighted result at 768 px and up. `facets` (`Facet`: `key`, `label`, `values`, `hint`) turn `key:value` tokens into removable chips and offer their values as you type; providers get `{ text, filters }`. While the query is empty it shows recent picks (kept under the app's storage prefix), `suggestions` and the facets. Arrow keys, Tab between groups, Enter, Escape, Backspace to take off a chip; every row 44 px or more.
`useSpotlight()`: the palette's open state and query in the URL (`?find=`), with ⌘K / Ctrl+K; spread its `bind` into `CommandPalette`.
`SearchTrigger` (a search-field-looking button that opens the palette) and `SearchIcon` (for the top-bar `TopBarButton` on phones).
`parseQuery` / `formatQuery`, and the types `SpotlightItem`, `SpotlightQuery`, `SpotlightFilter`, `SearchProvider`, `Facet`, `Suggestion`.
Guide section 9, *App-wide search*. The Style guide's CommandPalette block opens it from a `SearchTrigger`; the showcase searches its looks and backdrops (facets `set`, `tone`, `colours`, `group`).

No zoom in the installed app, like a native app: from the Home Screen, pinch-zoom and double-tap zoom are off. `foundation/src/lib/viewport.ts` (run by `applyTheme`) adds `maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no` to the viewport meta, sets `html[data-installed]` (`touch-action: pan-x pan-y` in `globals.css`) and cancels iOS's pinch gesture events. Browser tabs keep pinch-zoom. `isInstalledApp()` says which mode the app is in, and counts jimbo-deploy's iOS shell (`JimboShell` in the user agent) as installed.
Double-tap zoom is off everywhere (`touch-action: manipulation` on `html`), so taps are instant.
`CommandPalette` with only `commands` works as before; results now show each row's title in the body colour while highlighted, and a footer of key hints on wide screens.

`CommandPalette` `providers`, `facets`, `suggestions`, `recentKey`, `query` / `onQueryChange`; `useSpotlight`, `SearchTrigger`, `SearchIcon`, `parseQuery`, `formatQuery` (reference: copy `overlays.tsx` to adopt).

releases.summary: Space and Halloween: looks, two backdrop groups that keep moving on their own, and twelve motifs.

items.text: **Space** category on the Looks tab, with sub-tabs **Nebulae** (Stellar nursery, Pillars of dust, Veil), **Stars** (Red giant, Blue supergiant, White dwarf), **Planets** (Gas giant, Ringed world, Ice giant, Pale blue dot), **Deep sky** (Event horizon, Galaxy core, Launch window) and **Aurora** (Aurora, Solar wind, Midnight sun) — invented palettes, each with a style whose backdrop moves on its own.

**Halloween** category, with sub-tabs **Vampire** (Velvet coffin, Blood moon, Count's court, Crypt, Daybreak), **Haunted** (Haunted manor, Séance, Ectoplasm), **Witching** (Witching hour, Cauldron, Hex), **Graveyard** (Graveyard, Moonlit mist) and **Harvest** (Jack-o'-lantern, Candy corn, Harvest moon). The Holidays look stays. All 324 looks pass `contrast.mjs --check`.

**Cosmos** backdrop group: Starfield (twinkling), Nebula (clouds that swell and settle), Galaxy (a tilted spiral turning about its core), Orbits (planets going round a corner sun, each at its own pace), Aurora (curtains that fold and unfold), Comets (crossing on a diagonal), Constellations, Eclipse (a breathing, turning corona), Milky Way and Planetrise.

**Haunt** backdrop group: Bats (wings beating, drifting up), Webs (a spider riding its thread), Moonlit (clouds passing a full moon), Graveyard (fog drifting past headstones), Mist, Candles (flames flickering), Damask, Drips (now and then a drop falls), Briars (thorny vines swaying from the root) and Arches (pointed windows).
Motifs: **Planets**, **Comets**, **Suns**, **Rockets**, **Spirals**, **Bats**, **Pumpkins**, **Ghosts**, **Fangs**, **Coffins**, **Spiders** and **Drops**.

Alive motion can now be a pattern's own: a slow turn, a breath, a drift, a flicker or a planet's orbit, written into the pattern (`animatePattern` leaves open-and-closed elements alone). Some patterns twinkle instead of swaying (`TWINKLE`), some hold their shapes still and move only those parts (`HELD`). Corner art (a moon, a web, a sun) is sized to show whole on a phone and in a small tile.

appsMust: Nothing — copy the foundation files. The reference config section reads `BACKDROP_GROUPS`, `MOTIFS` and `FAMILY_SETS`, so the new categories, groups and motifs show up on their own.

releases.summary: The end of the world: apocalypse looks, a Ruin backdrop group and four new motifs.

items.text: **Apocalypse** category on the Looks tab, with sub-tabs **Nuclear** (Fallout shelter, Half-life, Nuclear winter), **Undead** (Outbreak, Dead of night, Quarantine), **Wasteland** (Dust bowl, Scorched earth, Rust belt), **Cosmic** (Last light, Impact, Judgement day) and **Collapse** (Drowned world, Wildfire smoke, Signal lost) — invented palettes, each in light, mid and dark, each with a style (heading font, backdrop, motif). All pass `contrast.mjs --check`.

**Ruin** backdrop group (fifth, after Texture): Embers (sparks rising when alive), Ash (flakes drifting down), Cracks, Hazard (caution stripes along the bottom), Skyline (a broken city), Fallout (scattered trefoils), Smog, Barbed (wire that slides along when alive), Static (scan lines over noise, rolling when alive) and Shockwave (broken rings that spread like Ripples).
Motifs: **Skulls**, **Trefoils**, **Flames** and **Hazards** — flat shapes like the rest.

appsMust: Nothing — copy the foundation files. The reference config section reads `BACKDROP_GROUPS`, `MOTIFS` and `FAMILY_SETS`, so the new tab, group and motifs show up on their own.

releases.summary: Retro console looks: eleven consoles' menus in colour, pattern and type.

items.text: **Consoles** sub-tab under Games on the Looks tab: PlayStation, Nintendo 64, Dreamcast, PlayStation 2, Xbox, GameCube, Game Boy Advance, PSP, Xbox 360, Wii and PlayStation 3, each from its hardware and menu colours (and shades of them), in light, mid and dark.

Looks can carry a **style** (`Template.style`, `TemplateStyle`: fonts, backdrop, motif). Each console look has one that calls up its menu — the PS2's drifting specks on blue-black, the GameCube's drifting cubes on indigo, the Xbox 360's slanted panels, the PS3's flowing lines — from jimbo-ui's own options, with no logos or system artwork. `TemplateFamily.style` and `familyAt` pass it on.
**Panels** backdrop (Abstract): tall slanted panels side by side; alive, each panel and its edge sway together.

Reference `ThemePanel`: picking a look with a style brings its font, backdrop and motif (a look without one keeps yours), and its card shows the backdrop and heading font. Optional to port — without it, console looks bring their colours only.

Page and section titles keep the heading weight, tracking and size again: `.font-display` is now a Tailwind `@utility`, so `@apply font-display` in `.h-page` and `.h-section` brings all three (under Tailwind 4 it copied only the font family). **Apps must:** Nothing — copy the foundation files.

releases.summary: Tailwind 4, and a round of new kit pieces: fields, menus, toasts, confirm, tables, steps and more.

items.text: **Forms** (`components/ui/forms.tsx`): `TextField` and `TextArea` (label, hint, inline error in the highlight colour; the area grows and counts down to a limit), `DateField` (the platform's own date and time pickers), `FileDrop` (pick or drop files; wrong types and sizes turned away with a reason).

**Overlays** (`components/ui/overlays.tsx`): `Menu` with the ⋯ `MoreButton` (full keyboard support), `Popover`, `Tooltip` (hover or keyboard focus only, never the only label), and `CommandPalette` + `useCommandPalette` (⌘K / Ctrl+K).

**Feedback** (`components/ui/feedback.tsx`): `toast()` + `Toaster` (above the dock; done, info, error; one action such as Undo), `ConfirmSheet` / `useConfirm` (one `await`), `ProgressBar` (promoted from candidate; also indeterminate), `Stepper`, `OfflineBanner` (the offline pattern as a component, with `useOnline`) and `UpdateBanner`.
**Data** (`components/ui/data.tsx`): `DataTable` (sortable on desktop, a row per record on phones, sort kept in the URL) and `Accordion` (native `<details>`).
Reference `AppShell` renders the `Toaster`. Layers 45 (menus, popovers, tooltips) and 60 (toasts).
The Style guide gets Forms, Menus and overlays, Feedback, and Tables and steps sections; the showcase opens the command palette from its search button and ⌘K.
Screenshot checks: `npm --prefix showcase run test:screens` captures every Style guide section at 375 px in a light, a mid and a dark look with Playwright and compares it with local baselines.

**Tailwind 4.** The theme moves from `tailwind.config.js` into `globals.css` (`@import "tailwindcss"` and `@theme inline`), so every colour and size utility follows the variables where it's used (a `ThemeScope`, a heading's `--fs`). It builds through `@tailwindcss/vite`, with no PostCSS. `tailwind-merge` goes to 3.
A bare `border` is the theme's line colour (Tailwind 4 would draw it in the text colour); buttons keep the pointer cursor.
`glass` is a Tailwind utility (`@utility`), so other classes can `@apply` it and it takes variants (`sm:glass`).
Kit utilities renamed for Tailwind 4: `outline-hidden`, `shadow-xs`, `backdrop-blur-xs`, `bg-linear-to-*`.
`foundation/tailwind.config.js`.

The legacy colour names from before 0.3: `accent-lime`, `accent-lime-hover`, `accent-pink`, `accent-pink-hover`, `accent-cyan`, `accent-cyan-hover`, `accent-orange`, `lime-700/900/950` and `rose-800/900/950`. **Apps must:** 1. Before copying anything, run `npx @tailwindcss/upgrade` in the web root. It renames utilities in the app's own code: `shadow-sm` → `shadow-xs`, `shadow` → `shadow-sm`, `blur-sm` → `blur-xs`, `outline-none` → `outline-hidden`, `ring` → `ring-3`, `bg-gradient-to-*` → `bg-linear-to-*`, and so on. 2. Install `tailwindcss@4`, `@tailwindcss/vite` and `tailwind-merge@3`; uninstall `autoprefixer` (and `postcss` if nothing else uses it). Delete `tailwind.config.js` and `postcss.config.js`, then add `tailwindcss()` from `@tailwindcss/vite` to the Vite plugins. 3. Copy the foundation files. The app's CSS entry keeps importing `globals.css`, which now brings in Tailwind. If the app keeps components in a folder git ignores, add `@source "<path>";` after that import. 4. Rename any legacy colour names: `accent-lime` → `accent`, `accent-pink` → `highlight`, `lime-*` → `accent-*`, `rose-*` → `highlight-*`. Replace `accent-cyan` / `accent-orange` with a theme colour. 5. In the app's own CSS, `@apply` works only on utilities now. Replace `@apply card` (or another kit component class) with the class in markup. A CSS file that uses `@apply` without importing `globals.css` needs `@reference "<path to globals.css>";` at the top. 6. Optional: copy `forms.tsx`, `overlays.tsx`, `feedback.tsx` and `data.tsx` into `components/ui/`, and add `<Toaster />` to the app shell (reference `AppShell.tsx`) before using `toast()`. 7. Typecheck, build, and check pages at 375 px in a dark, a mid and a light look.

releases.summary: The motif saves, backdrop patterns move line by line, the favicon is the motif, and Marcone and mSupply are separate looks in their own colours.

items.text: **Alive** backdrop motion: each pattern moves its own way, line by line. Rain falls, confetti drifts down, arrows rise, stripes slide (a tile at a time, so the loop never jumps), ripples spread, and every other line or shape sways on its own path and timing. It's SMIL inside the pattern's SVG (`animatePattern`), drawn still for people who ask for reduced motion.
`motifFavicon`: the built-in favicon is one of the theme's motif shape in the accent on the page colour, drawn from the theme.
**Pulse** fades each line and shape on its own beat instead of the whole backdrop together. Motion options are a grid (Still, Alive, Pulse, Drift, Breathe, Sway) so they fit on phones.

**Brands:** Marcone and mSupply are separate looks, using only colours from their own websites. Marcone is logo red `#D22630` on white or black. mSupply is navy `#1B365D` on white. Missing roles are shades of the accent (`infer: "tonal"`), not new hues. Guide: a theme has up to four colours, and a brand with one stays one.
Guide: the server stores the theme object as sent, not a list of known fields.
`themedFavicon`: the built-in favicon is `motifFavicon` now.
**The motif didn't save:** `withDefaults` (reference `useBrand.ts`) rebuilt the saved theme field by field and dropped `motif`. It now passes every saved field through, so new theme options save too.
**Favicon broken** where `/favicon.svg` isn't at the site root (the showcase page): `applyFavicon` no longer fetches a file, and adds the icon link if the page has none.

appsMust: Copy the foundation files.
Port `withDefaults` from `reference/web/src/lib/useBrand.ts`, and make the server store and return the whole theme object (`PUT /admin/theme`), so the motif and backdrop motion save.
Replace `public/favicon.svg` with the starter's (one accent circle on the page colour, in the app's default colours). Port the Backdrop tab's motion grid from `config/ThemePanel.tsx`.

releases.summary: Nintendo, Sly Cooper and Tony Hawk's Underground looks, motif shapes (a triforce among them), slow backdrop motion, calmer fonts, and the view kept in the URL.

items.text: **Game looks:** the Games category gets sub-tabs, one per series. New: **Super Mario** (Mario, Luigi, Princess Peach, Bowser, Toad, Wario, Yoshi, Yoshi's Island), **Donkey Kong** (Donkey Kong, Diddy Kong, Donkey Kong Country, the 1981 arcade), **More Nintendo** (Kirby, Metroid, Star Fox, Pikmin, Splatoon), **Sly Cooper** (Sly Cooper, Bentley, Murray, Carmelita Fox, Thievius Raccoonus) and **Tony Hawk's Underground**, its menu themes (T.H.U.G., Cloudbuster, Retro Hawk, Chilled, Skullz 'N Stuff). Colours only, made with `template-from-colours.mjs`; every one passes the contrast check in light, mid and dark.

**Motif shapes** (`Theme.motif`, `MOTIFS`, `motifMask`): `ThemeDots` draws the theme's colours as circles (the default) or as triforces, sparkles, stars, hearts, diamonds, triangles, squares, crosses, bolts, flowers, moons or squiggles, using `.motif-accent/highlight/support` and the `--motif-mask` CSS variable. Flat, side by side, at the circles' fixed sizes. Status dots, avatars and swatches stay circles. It's picked on the config section's Brand tab and is part of the theme draft, its export and `tokens.css`.

**Backdrop motion** (`backdrop.motion`, `backdrop.speed`, `BACKDROP_MOTIONS`, `backdropAnimation`): still (the default), drift, breathe, sway or pulse, slowly, at 0.5–2× speed. It's a CSS animation of the backdrop layer (`--bg-animation`, keyframes `jimbo-bg-*` in `globals.css`), and it's off for people who ask for reduced motion. It's on the Backdrop tab.
**`useUrlState` / `useUrlNumber` / `setUrlParams`** (reference `lib/useUrlState.ts`): view state as a search parameter that replaces the history entry and drops out at its default.
**Fonts:** Geist and Plus Jakarta (sans), Newsreader, Literata and Instrument Serif (serif), Bebas Neue, Unbounded and Syne (decorative).

**The URL holds the view** (guide section 6): routes in the URL, and tabs, sub-tabs, filters, searches, pages and an open item as search parameters. The reference config section keeps its tab, the Looks category, sub-tab, tone and search, the backdrop group, the font groups and the Style guide section in the URL. The catalogue archetype keeps its search, filter, page and chosen place there, and the status archetype its range.

Showcase: the Archetypes tab is gone, and Home is the hero plus every component. The route is in the URL (`#/jimbo-ui?tab=type`, `HashRouter` instead of `MemoryRouter`), so a refresh or Back keeps the view, and an unknown route goes home. Random looks take a random motif too.

**Fonts:** IBM Plex Sans, Work Sans, Fraunces, Marcellus, Cormorant, Rocker, Uncial and Carved caps (Cinzel). A saved theme that used one gets the nearest that's left (`RETIRED_FONTS`: Geist, Plus Jakarta, Newsreader, Literata, EB Garamond, Gothic, Old print, Instrument Serif). The old `serif` style name now means Newsreader headings.
`Theme.motif`, `.motif-*`, `MotifPanel`; `backdrop.motion` and `speed`; `useUrlState`

appsMust: Use `BrowserRouter` (never `MemoryRouter`) and move view state into the URL with `useUrlState` / `useUrlNumber`: tabs, sub-tabs, segmented controls, filters, sorts, searches, page numbers and an open item or sheet. Copy `reference/web/src/lib/useUrlState.ts`, then port `JimboConfigPage.tsx`, `config/ThemePanel.tsx` and `config/StyleGuidePanel.tsx` (the motif picker and motion controls come with them).
Copy the foundation files. If `index.html` or `tokens.css` names a removed font, switch it to its replacement (above) and regenerate `tokens.css` with `scripts/tokens.mjs`.
Use `ThemeDots` for the motif rather than hand-made rows of `.dot-*` circles, so the theme's shape shows.

releases.summary: The paper backdrop no longer repeats in a visible grid, and a hero with no pattern lets the page's backdrop run through.

items.text: **Paper backdrop** no longer repeats in a visible grid: two noise layers with different seeds at sizes that don't line up (1100 and 737 px) instead of one 420 px tile.
**`HeroSection pattern="none"`** draws no layer of its own, so the page's backdrop runs straight through instead of a faded band across it.

appsMust: Nothing — copy the foundation files. Apps with a `HeroSection pattern="none"` port it from `reference/web/src/components/ui/kit.tsx`.

releases.summary: Solid fills with no outline, glass on anything over the backdrop, Style guide sections, and a showcase where random looks take turns over every component.

items.text: **Style guide sections** (reference `StyleGuidePanel`): the blocks sit in five sections — Brand and type, Controls, Numbers and charts, Lists, States — with toggles at the top, one shown at a time instead of one long page. An app adds its own domain components as extra sections with `more={[{ value, label, content }]}`.

**Solid fills, no outlines:** `.lit-*` and `.btn-primary` drop their darker inner outline — one flat colour. Selected `PillTabs`, `ToggleGrid` picks, `SwitchRow` switches and row ticks are the solid fill with no coloured border, and the dock's active tab is a solid accent fill instead of a tint with an outline.

**Glass on the backdrop:** unselected `PillTabs` are `.glass` (frosted, blurred) instead of a bare outline, so their text keeps its contrast over any backdrop pattern. Guide: anything sitting straight on the backdrop is `.glass`.

Showcase: Home has it all now. Ten looks picked at random on each load (a random tone, fonts and backdrop for each) take turns on the whole page — colours, type, backdrop, the hero and the map — every 15 seconds, fading slowly (1.2 s) from the last. A small control sits top right above the hero and sticks under the bar as the page scrolls (on phones as a full-width frosted strip, so it never covers content): the look's name and a countdown to the next, arrows to step (← → keys too) that pause the timer, play / pause, and *Use* to keep one. It's a preview until then, and leaving Home puts the saved look back. Below it, every component in the section toggles, plus Maps and Release updates. The Components tab is gone (its old link lands on Home).
`StyleGuidePanel` sections and its `more` prop

appsMust: Nothing — copy the foundation files (the flat `.lit-*` and `.btn-primary` come with them). Apps that want the sections, the glass pills and the solid selected states port `StyleGuidePanel.tsx`, and the `PillTabs`, `ToggleGrid`, `SwitchRow`, row-tick and dock-tab classes from `kit.tsx` and `AppShell.tsx` in `reference/web/src/`.

releases.summary: The showcase steps through its looks with Previous and Next, each fading slowly into the next.

items.text: Showcase: the front page's looks no longer play as a carousel. **Previous** and **Next** step through them, each look fading slowly (1.2 s) into the next; the dots and Play / Pause are gone.

appsMust: Nothing — copy the foundation files.

releases.summary: Three components from jimbo-theory join the kit, and EntityRow can show a code in its avatar.

items.text: **`ToggleGrid`** (kit): several picks from a small fixed set as a wrapping grid of 44 px toggle buttons (`columns`, `smColumns`), picked ones a flat accent fill with `aria-pressed`.
**`LinkChips`** (kit): related things as a wrapping row of linked chips, each with an optional muted second label and an 8 px dot in a theme colour.
**`FloatingBar`** (kit): a status line and its actions floating above the dock, with an optional pulsing `live` dot. The theme save bar now uses it.
**`EntityRow avatarText`**: the placeholder avatar shows a short code or number instead of the name's initials.
Guide: section 8 rows for the three, and "Picking several" and "Related things" in the component menu. The Style guide panel shows them.
`ToggleGrid`, `LinkChips`, `FloatingBar`, `EntityRow avatarText`

appsMust: Nothing — copy the foundation files. Apps that want them port them from `reference/web/src/components/ui/kit.tsx` (jimbo-theory has its own copies of ToggleGrid and LinkChips and an equivalent practice bar to swap for these).

releases.summary: The version number now says what an update takes: a new 0.MINOR needs code changes, a 0.x.PATCH is drop-in.

items.text: **The number says what an update takes.** Numbering follows Semantic Versioning read for 0.x: a **breaking** release (apps change their own code) is the next 0.MINOR; a **feature** or **fix** release (drop-in) is the next 0.x.PATCH; from 1.0.0, MAJOR / MINOR / PATCH. Every entry here now has an **Update:** line, and the head of this file explains it.
The update workflow takes an update within the app's 0.MINOR straight through (copy the foundation files, set the version) and previews a breaking one before touching the app's code.
`scripts/versions.mjs` fails a release numbered too low for its type, and `--next` gives the number Unreleased needs.

`releases.json` gives each release's `type`; the session-start check says whether an update is drop-in or needs code changes, and the config section's About tab badges each release (Code changes, New, Fixes) and says which the whole update is (`Release.type`, `Updates.breaking` in `jimbo.ts`).

appsMust: Nothing — copy the foundation files. Port `routes/config/UpdatesPanel.tsx` to see the update type in the About tab.

releases.summary: Each app's details live only in its own jimbo-ui.json; jimbo-ui keeps just the list of apps and its component catalogue.

items.text: **Each fact in one place.** An app's details — version, auth, web root, the components it uses and its own — live only in its `jimbo-ui.json`. `registry/apps.json` is just each app's name, repo and registration date; `registry/components.json` is jimbo-ui's catalogue (shared components and generic candidates, no `usedBy`, no app-only entries or app-specific aliases). App sessions no longer commit to jimbo-ui when they update or consolidate.

`scripts/inventory.mjs` puts the registry together from the apps: each app's `jimbo-ui.json` as pushed (read with `gh`), its checkout for the code checks (`~/Development`, `--apps-dir` or `JIMBO_APPS_DIRS`), a warning when a checkout is stale, and `--json` for the assembled registry.
The scan for app words now covers the catalogue too; only `registry/apps.json` is skipped.

appsMust: Keep `components` in `jimbo-ui.json` current (`uses`, and `local` with each piece's kind and the catalogue id it matches) — it's the only record. An app with no `components` yet runs "Consolidate an app".
Update the jimbo-ui block in the app's `CLAUDE.md` to the new wording in SKILL.md ("Register an app", step 8).

releases.summary: Nine fonts per group with a size for headings and body, twelve backdrops per group, a themed iOS icon, a Brands category and a Status monitor archetype.

items.text: **Text size for headings and body** (`fonts.headingsSize`, `fonts.bodySize`, 0.8–1.3; the Type tab's *Size* slider, shown as ± em). Every Tailwind text size is now its usual size × `--fs` (the body size, or the headings size inside `.font-display`), with ratio line heights, so the whole scale moves together. Named pixel sizes `text-7` … `text-40` replace the kit's `text-[Npx]`.

**Fonts, nine per group:** IBM Plex Sans, Work Sans, Avenir (Avenir Next or Avenir on Apple devices, Nunito Sans elsewhere), Figtree; Baskerville, Cormorant, Lora; Roboto Mono, Source Code, DM Mono, Red Hat Mono, Inconsolata; Old print, Uncial.

**Backdrops, twelve per group** (48): Abstract adds swirl, ribbons, scribble, rain; Geo adds squares, zigzag, rings, crosses, scales, cubes, checks; Vintage adds pinstripe, gingham, polka, plaid, argyle, racing stripes, trellis, bauhaus; Texture adds concrete, brushed, sand, speckle, crosshatch, twill, carbon, ribbed.

**Status monitor archetype** (`reference/web/src/archetypes/status.tsx`, on the showcase's Archetypes tab): the services you run, whether each is up, how fast it answers and how it's reached, recent checks as a row of dots, an Open button, and history charts over a range. From auditing the registered apps: the catalogue and the single-page dashboard already cover the other two.

**Brands** category on the Looks tab: companies' own palettes, colours only. First, **Marcone** — Pantone 1795 red with its parent mSupply's navy — written light and dark, mid made from its own colours.

**The iOS home-screen icon follows the theme.** `applyFavicon` draws the recoloured favicon (or an uploaded one) as a 180 px PNG on the theme's background and points `apple-touch-icon` at it (`themedFavicon`, `iconPng` in `theme.ts`). iOS keeps the icon from when the app was added, so a phone that already has it needs to remove it and add it again.
Fonts Oswald, Pixel, Bungee, Neon and Script. A saved theme that used one falls back to Archivo for headings and Inter for body.
Showcase: the home hero draws no pattern of its own over the page's backdrop, and the look carousel keeps one height on every slide.

appsMust: Copy the foundation files (theme, `globals.css`, Tailwind config) and port the kit and config panels (they use `text-15` and friends).
Replace `text-[Npx]` in the app's own code with the named size (`text-15`), or add the size to the Tailwind config, so it follows the theme's size.
If the app's default theme used a removed font, pick another.
Keep `<link rel="apple-touch-icon" …>` in `index.html` (the reference has it); `applyFavicon` replaces its picture at runtime.

releases.summary: Apps say when a newer jimbo-ui is out and what updating would change; the Theme tab is now Looks, Colours, Type and Backdrop.

items.text: **Apps say when a newer jimbo-ui is out.** The About tab of the jimbo-ui config section (`JimboUpdates`, `useJimboUpdates` in `reference/web/src/routes/config/UpdatesPanel.tsx`) lists the newer releases and sorts what updating would change for the app: to do in its own code (**Apps must**), changes to kit components it uses (from `jimbo-ui.json` `components.uses`), what comes with the foundation, and what's new if it wants it — with the request to paste into the app's Claude session. `JimboConfigLink` shows "jimbo-ui X is out" and opens About. Read from GitHub at most once a day per person, only for people who can configure; nothing extra shows when it can't be reached.

**`releases.json`**, written from this changelog by `scripts/releases.mjs` at each release: every release, its items by kind, the components each names (matched against the registry) and its Apps must. `scripts/versions.mjs` checks it's current.
`foundation/src/lib/jimbo.ts`: `JIMBO_UI.releases` and `.changelog`, `fetchReleases`, `updatesFor`, `compareVersions` and their types.
The showcase's Components tab shows the update check for an app that's current, one release behind and four behind.

**The Theme tab is now four tabs:** Looks (templates and *Share this look*), Colours, Type and Backdrop, so no tab is a long page of everything. They edit one unsaved look (`useThemeDraft`, held by `JimboConfigPage`) with one save bar (`ThemeSaveBar`) over every tab. `?tab=theme` still opens Looks.
The config section's tabs sit on one row that scrolls sideways on phones, with the chosen one kept in view: `PillTabs scroll`.

appsMust: Port `routes/config/ThemePanel.tsx` (it now exports `LooksPanel`, `ColoursPanel`, `TypePanel`, `BackdropPanel`, `ThemeSaveBar` and `useThemeDraft` instead of `ThemePanel`) and `PillTabs` from the kit. An app that links to the section's colours, type or backdrop can use `?tab=colours`, `type` or `backdrop`.
Copy the foundation files, port `JimboConfigPage.tsx` and add `routes/config/UpdatesPanel.tsx` from the reference.
Keep `components.uses` in `jimbo-ui.json` current; it decides which changes count as the app's.
If the app has a Content Security Policy, allow `https://raw.githubusercontent.com` in `connect-src`.

releases.summary: Openers fade into the page (no hard edge under banners and heroes), plus charts and rows-or-tiles lists.

items.text: **Charts.** `TrendChart` (one to three lines over time, a crosshair you tap, drag or arrow-key, and a readout that names each series), `BarChart` (horizontal rows or vertical columns — promoted from the `bar-chart` candidate), `Sparkline`, and a `trend` prop on `StatTile`. Flat SVG in the theme's colours, with a hidden table of the numbers for screen readers. The guide's new Charts pattern says when to use which.

**Rows or tiles.** `List layout="tiles"` shows the same children as a grid of cards; `LayoutSwitch` and `useListLayout` let people pick and remember it. Supporting variants: `Section plain` (no card, for tiles under a title), `Tabs size="sm"` (a compact switch for a section's action slot), `List bare` (no card, inside `Section flush`).

Both dashboard archetypes use them: the single-page dashboard template has sparklines on its stats, a jobs list you can switch to tiles, and a bar chart and a trend chart. The Style guide panel shows every chart and the tiles layout.
`TrendChart`, `BarChart`, `Sparkline`, `StatTile trend`, `List layout`, `LayoutSwitch`, `useListLayout`, `Section plain`, `Tabs size="sm"` — in the reference kit; port them when an app wants them.

`divide-etched` reached into every `<div>` child, so a row built as a `<div>` (a job row, a `KeyValue`) got a stray divider line inside it. It now only reaches into list groups — a wrapper that starts with a `ListGroupLabel`, which carries a new `list-group-label` class.

**No more hard edge under banners and heroes.** `Banner` (and `Hero`) and `HeroSection` faded to solid page colour, or ended on a border, so over a page backdrop they stopped on a visible line. Their background layer now fades out to transparent (`.fade-out` in `globals.css`; `.fade-both` also fades the top when something sits above), letting the page's backdrop show through.

`HeroSection`, `Banner` and `Hero` tucked up under the top bar even when something sat above them, covering it (the showcase's catalogue tabs). They take `pullUp={false}` for that case; the default is unchanged.

appsMust: Copy the foundation files (`globals.css` has `.fade-out`), and port `Banner` and `HeroSection` from the reference kit.

Any page header of the app's own with a blurred photo or gradient behind it (a year or profile header, say): move that background into its own layer behind the content, give the layer `fade-out`, and remove any border under it or fade to `bg`.
Pass `pullUp={false}` only where something sits above a hero.

Port `ListGroupLabel` from the reference kit (it adds the `list-group-label` class); without it, grouped lists lose the dividers between their rows. Any workaround for the stray line (rows as `<article>` rather than `<div>`) can go.

releases.summary: Fix: pages that fill the screen with `min-h-full` (sign-in screens) work again.

items.text: `globals.css`: `html`, `body` and `#root` are `height: 100%` again. 0.8.1 made `body` and `#root` a minimum height only, so `h-full` / `min-h-full` inside them shrank to their content and centred screens sat at the top. `#root` keeps its `100dvh` minimum.

releases.summary: A solid status bar on installed apps, so iOS's top-edge blur no longer covers the header.

items.text: **Status bar:** `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style` is `default`, not `black-translucent`. Since iOS 26.1 an installed app with a translucent status bar gets a system blur over the status bar and the top of the page that the page can't turn off; it covered the app's name. With `default`, iOS draws a solid status bar in the `theme-color` (the theme's background, which `applyTheme` already sets) and the page starts below it.
`scripts/inventory.mjs` flags apps whose status bar isn't `default`.

appsMust: Set `<meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style" content="default" />` in `index.html` (as `reference/web/index.html`), and keep the `theme-color` meta with the pre-paint script that sets it.
Remove the app from the Home Screen and add it again on each phone: iOS reads the status bar style only when it's added.

releases.summary: Full screen on phones: pages fill the screen and nothing sits under the status bar.

items.text: **Full screen on phones.** Layouts fill the screen edge to edge and top to bottom, and nothing sits under the status bar's blur or the home indicator. The page colour is on `html`; the backdrop is a fixed layer the full height of the screen (`body::before`) instead of a body background (iOS ignored `background-attachment: fixed`, so it scrolled and stopped short); `body` and `#root` are at least `100dvh`.
`AppShell`, `Sheet`, the image viewer, `MapView`, the catalogue archetype and the theme panel's save bar use the new safe-area variables instead of `env()`.
**Safe-area variables** in `globals.css`: `--safe-top`, `--safe-bottom`, `--safe-left`, `--safe-right`, `--top-bar`, `--dock-space`, `--above-dock`.

`foundation/src/lib/viewport.ts`: `applyTheme` makes sure the viewport meta has `viewport-fit=cover` (an installed app without it draws under the status bar while its insets read 0) and warns in development.
`scripts/inventory.mjs` reports each app's phone frame: `viewport-fit`, status bar style and raw `env(safe-area-…)` in app code.

appsMust: Have `viewport-fit=cover` and `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style` `black-translucent` in `index.html` (as `reference/web/index.html`).
Drop any `bg-*` or `background-attachment` the app sets on `body` for the backdrop; the foundation draws it.

Replace `env(safe-area-inset-…)` in their own code with the variables (`pt-[var(--safe-top)]`, `bottom-[var(--above-dock)]`, …), and pad any bar of their own that's fixed to the top of the screen by `--safe-top`.
Re-copy `AppShell` (or apply its changes: header `pt-[var(--safe-top)]`, main `pb-[var(--dock-space)]`, root `min-h-[100dvh]`).
Check at 375 px as an installed app: the app's name is clear of the status bar and the page reaches the bottom of the screen.

releases.summary: One library with no duplicates, one jimbo-ui config section per app, every look in light, mid and dark, 21 backdrops, maps in the theme, and two archetypes to copy.

items.text: **Registry:** `registry/apps.json` (every app on jimbo-ui: repo, web root, version, auth, registered, last audited) and `registry/components.json` (every UI element across all apps: id, name, purpose, tier — foundation, kit, pattern, candidate or domain — source, usedBy, aliases, variants). Names and paths only, never app code.

**Dedupe rules** (guide section 13): match by purpose and behaviour, not name; a match is that component (an alias, maybe a variant prop), never a second one; promote at two apps or when clearly generic; domain pieces stay in their app; pull before writing to the registry.

**`scripts/inventory.mjs`:** component × app table, candidates built by more than one app, unused kit components, apps behind, raw colours in app code, and config sections that are missing, split up or gated wrong.

**The jimbo-ui config section** (`reference/web/src/routes/JimboConfigPage.tsx`): one place at `/jimbo-ui` with Theme, Brand, Style guide, About and an optional App tab, gated by `canConfigure`; `JimboConfigLink` for the app's settings. The old Brand and Style guide pages are now its panels (`routes/config/ThemePanel.tsx`, `routes/config/StyleGuidePanel.tsx`).

**`MapView` and `MapPinCard`** (`reference/web/src/components/MapView.tsx`): every map in the theme's style with flat highlight pins; a themed preview when there's no Maps key. Needs `@vis.gl/react-google-maps`.
**`ThemeScope`** (kit) and **`themeVars`** (`theme.ts`): theme part of a page — colours, type and backdrop — without touching the rest; `.theme-scope` in `globals.css`.

**Archetypes as templates:** `reference/web/src/archetypes/catalogue.tsx` (Home · Entries · People · Places, with a map) and `dashboard.tsx` (a single-page dashboard of jobs, runs and settings), to copy and remix.
`foundation/src/lib/jimbo.ts`: the release's version and links (`JIMBO_UI`), and the app's `jimbo-ui.json` when Vite passes it in (`__JIMBO_APP__`) for the About tab.
`jimbo-ui.json` gains `auth` (`"admin"` or `"none"`), `registry` and `components` (`uses`, `local`, `overrides`).
Skill workflows **Register an app** and **Consolidate an app**, with their trigger phrases.

**Every look in light, mid and dark:** each palette, team, flag or game is one tile (`FAMILY_SETS`, `TemplateFamily`), and a Light / Mid / Dark switch sets the page tone every tile shows. Tones a look wasn't written in are made from its own colours (`atTone`, `familyAt`, `familyLook`); every look passes the checks in every tone it's shown in (237 looks, 332 made tones). `toneOf`, `PAGE_TONES`, `templateScores`, `templateIssues` in `theme.ts`; `scripts/contrast.mjs` now checks every look in every tone.
**Games** category: twelve Legend of Zelda palettes, from the 1986 original to Echoes of Wisdom.

**Backdrops in four groups** (`BACKDROP_GROUPS`): Abstract (adds blobs, flow, confetti), Geo (adds hexagons, diamonds, grid), Vintage (halftone, retro stripes, sunburst, deco fans) and Texture (adds grain, paper, linen) — 21 patterns. New `Backdrop.contrast` (how far the pattern stands out) and `Backdrop.saturation` (its colour, down to greys) sliders.
**`KeyValue`** — a read-only label and value, `inline` or `stacked`.
**`SwitchRow`** — one setting on or off, the whole row the switch.
**`Autocomplete`** — pick an existing record as you type, or add one.
**`Badge dot` / `live`** — a status dot in the chip, pulsing while live.
**`EventRow onOpen`** — open something in place instead of a link; and **`RowStatus.live`** / **`LIVE`** — a status dot that pulses while running.

The showcase opens on a hero with a carousel of looks (each slide a piece of the kit in its own theme, font and backdrop); its tabs are Home, Components, Archetypes and Settings, with the jimbo-ui config section under Settings.
`applyTheme` uses `themeVars`; no change to what it sets.

The Theme tab: Everyday's Dark, Mid and Light lists are one list, and sports teams' Home / Away / Retro switch is gone — the tone switch covers it (a team's away look is its light tone). Retro looks are their own tiles.
The separate Brand & theme (`/admin/brand`) and Style guide (`/admin/style`) pages, as pages — they live on as the config section's tabs.

appsMust: **Adopt the jimbo-ui config section:** port `JimboConfigPage.tsx` and `routes/config/` from the reference; route it at `/jimbo-ui`; put `JimboConfigLink` in the app's settings or admin area (not the dock). Move every brand, theme and style guide option into it (app-specific extras go in its App tab) and remove `/admin/brand`, `/admin/style` and any other theme pickers or links to them.

**Gate it by `auth`:** add `"auth"` to `jimbo-ui.json`. With `"admin"`, pass `canConfigure={user?.isAdmin}` (the route redirects everyone else, the link doesn't render) and make sure every server route that saves the theme or brand checks admin on the server. With `"none"`, pass `canConfigure`.
Pass the app's `jimbo-ui.json` to the About tab: in `vite.config.ts`, `define: { __JIMBO_APP__: JSON.stringify({ name, ...jimboUiJson }) }`.
If the app shows a map: use `MapView` (and `MapPinCard` on a map page) instead of its own.

Port the Theme tab's template grid from `routes/config/ThemePanel.tsx` (families with the Light / Mid / Dark switch) and its grouped backdrop picker with the contrast and saturation sliders. Saved themes still load as they are.
Nothing for the promoted components — use them when you consolidate.
Get registered: "register this app with jimbo-ui" (fills `components` and the registry); later, "consolidate this app with jimbo-ui".

releases.summary: Clearer separation, a calmer surface (less glass, less round, flat swatches), fonts and sliders, and themes for teams and places.

items.text: **Templates from real colours (314):** every NHL, NBA, MLB and NFL team in a **Home** look (its colour) and an **Away** look (white; baseball road grey); Toronto, Ottawa and Chicago teams in other leagues (MLS, CFL, WNBA, PWHL, NWSL, CPL, NLL, AHL, OHL), also home and away; **Retro** looks for Toronto and Ottawa (St. Pats, Raptors ’95, Blue Jays ’77, Original Senators, Senators ’92, Rough Riders); 17 more countries; Canada's 13 provinces and territories on their flags' field colours. They use **only their own colours** and shades of them — no invented hues, no reds turned pink. 363 templates in all, every one passing the checks. `Template.kit`.
**Pilot** template (Everyday · Dark): the pilot app's original palette — lime, hot pink and cyan on near-black.

**Backdrops:** `Theme.backdrop` — an abstract pattern (ripples, waves, contours, geometry, light burst, dot grid, arrows, shapes, or none) over a base (solid, gradient, or the glow orbs as before), with strength and size. `backdropCss`, `BACKDROPS`, `BACKDROP_BASES`; set as `--bg-image` / `--bg-size` / `--bg-position` / `--bg-repeat` (pre-paint applies them). A *Backdrop* section on the Brand page with a preview of each pattern. Exports and imports carry the backdrop; templates keep it.

**Full width:** `FullBleed` (any section edge to edge, in a tone or flush), `HeroSection` (a full-width opener over a pattern, no photo) and `AppShell width` (`column` · `wide` · `full`). The showcase home opens with a `HeroSection` and has a full-width band.
**The component menu (skill and guide):** before building a feature or section, ask which existing component to use, from a menu of options.

**App archetypes (skill and guide):** Tracker, Collection, Dashboard, Directory, Planner, Showcase and Tool — each with dock tabs, page width, the components for its main pages and a backdrop. Starting an app asks which fits first.

**Share this look (import / export):** the Brand page exports the theme being edited as a theme file (`jimbo-ui/theme` JSON), the app's `brand.config.ts` `defaultTheme` line or its `tokens.css`, and imports a theme file to preview it — so the showcase works as a playground for designing a theme for any app, and themes move between apps. Helpers in `theme.ts`: `exportTheme`, `importTheme`, `brandConfigLine`, `tokensCss` (`scripts/tokens.mjs` now prints `tokensCss`).

**Docker:** `compose.yaml` and `showcase/Dockerfile` run the showcase as a local web app — `docker compose up --build` (nginx, port 4460) or `docker compose --profile dev up` (live reload, port 4461).

**Tonal inference:** `Theme.infer: "tonal"` fills a missing highlight or support with lighter or darker versions of the accent (the default, `"contrast"`, picks new hues). The Brand page has a *Contrasting / Tonal* switch. `deltaE` is exported.

**Vibrancy and contrast:** `Theme.vibrancy` (0.4–1.5) scales the brand colours' saturation; `Theme.contrast` (0.8–1.6) scales how far cards, fields and borders step from the page. Sliders on the Brand page.

**Fonts:** 25 in `FONTS` — sans (Archivo, Inter, Space Grotesk, DM Sans, Manrope, Oswald), serif (Fraunces, Source Serif, Playfair, EB Garamond, Marcellus — the closest free match to Friz Quadrata — DM Serif), mono (JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Mono, Space Mono, Fira Code) and decorative, for headings only (Old English, Old German, Gothic, Pirate, Rocker, Typewriter, Pixel, Bungee, Neon, Carved caps, Script). `Theme.fonts` takes a font key for headings and body plus `headingsWeight`, `bodyWeight`, `headingsTracking`, `bodyTracking`, set as `--font-display-weight` / `--font-body-weight` / `-tracking`. Weight and letter-spacing sliders (`RangeField`, kit). Old style names (`sans`, `mono`, `serif`) still work.

**Categories:** Everyday, Holidays, Countries (Americas, Europe, Asia and Pacific, Africa), Provinces, Sports (sub-tabs: NHL, NBA, MLB, NFL, Toronto, Ottawa, Chicago — city tabs gather every team from that city). `TemplateSet.tabs` shows a category's groups as sub-tabs; `ALL_TEMPLATES` lists every template once.
**Search** on the Brand page across name, vibe, category and tab, ignoring accents.
`scripts/template-from-colours.mjs`: real colours in (with an optional page colour, light or road-grey page, and kit), checked templates out.

**Circles are flat, side by side, at fixed sizes.** Every circle is one solid fill — no outline, ring, gradient, glow or shadow, and no orbs: the blurred colour blobs behind a photo-less `Banner` are gone. `ThemeDots` are 8 px dots side by side with a 4 px gap (they overlapped with a ring); status dots, label dots, avatars and swatches lose their outlines; inferred swatches show faded instead of dash-ringed; the page-colour swatch keeps a hairline border. New `.dot-accent/highlight/support` (`.orb-*` stay as older names). The guide spells out the rules (section 2, Circles).
"Flags" is now **Countries**, grouped by region.
**The separation check allows tonal themes:** accent and highlight at least 15 apart (ΔE), and no two of the three closer than 10 (was 20 for all).
Sweden, the Maple Leafs and other two-colour brands are shades of their colours rather than borrowing an inferred one; the steel-blue support for black-and-silver teams is gone (greys instead).
The Brand page picks categories with wrapping `PillTabs` (sub-tabs in a panel below) instead of `Tabs`, so five or more never scroll sideways.
`scripts/contrast.mjs` checks each template once (city tabs repeat league teams).

**Every app has the admin theming pages.** The skill and guide now require a Brand & theme page and a Style guide in every app, nearly identical to the reference and adapted only to the app (access, who may save, where it saves, copy, its own components). An app without a server keeps the page and saves the theme in the browser (like the showcase's `api.ts`) instead of dropping it. The start, preview and update workflows check for every theming feature. The theme API carries `fonts`.
**No dots above page titles.** `PageHeader` eyebrows are plain support text again; `ThemeDots` stays for empty states.

**Flat fills everywhere.** `.btn-primary` and `.lit-*` (active tabs and pills, select ticks, date bands, the top bar's add button) are flat with a slight outline in the colour's darker shade — no gradient, top highlight or glow; `.btn-secondary`, `.glass` and the dock lose their top highlight; the active dock tab is a flat `accent/15` with an outline.

**Flat swatches.** Colour circles are flat with a slight outline in their own darker shade — no sphere shading or glow: `.orb-*`, `EntityRow` avatars (now `orb-support` with `on-support` text), status dots (`STATUS_DOT` is a 10 px flat dot with a faint dark ring; `TONES[*].dot` is just the fill again), and the Brand page's theme-tile and editor swatches.
**Less glassy.** `.glass` is mostly solid (`bg-surface/90`, `blur-md`, `border-border`); the top bar, dock, view switch and sheets are solid or near-solid; cards are 97% opaque.

**Less round, not flat.** Radius scale: cards 14 px (was 18), fields 11 (14), sheets 18 (24), dock 20 (28), active dock tab 14 (22). Buttons and pill tabs use the new `rounded-control` (10 px) instead of full pills; chips 8, tabs 8, badges 6. Circles stay round (avatars, dots, orbs, round icon buttons). Lit fills and shadows stay.

**Stronger lines and layers.** `CONTRAST_TARGETS`: borders step to 1.8:1 against cards (was 1.55), cards to 1.2:1 against the page (was 1.16), fields and chips to 1.15:1 against cards (was 1.14). The contrast report now requires border ≥ 1.75 and card ≥ 1.19; every template passes.
Rows are a little taller (`py-3.5`, at least 76 px).

**Type section:** `Theme.fonts` (see Fonts above), set as `--font-display` and `--font-body`, which Tailwind's `font-display` / `font-body` now read. `FONTS`, `FONT_GROUPS`, `fontFor`, `loadFonts`. Brand page gains a *Type* section; templates keep the chosen fonts. `scripts/tokens.mjs --headings= --body=` (font keys). `SavedTheme` type for API data.
`.divide-etched`: a full-strength line with a faint light line under it between stacked items; it also reaches rows grouped in wrappers under a label. `List`, `RankedList` and `Loading` use it.

**A changed theme showed up late.** `useBrand` treated the cached theme as fresh for 5 minutes on every load, so a new look (or one changed on another device) could take that long to appear. The cached copy still paints at once but is marked old (`initialDataUpdatedAt: 0`), so the server's theme is fetched straight away.

appsMust: Apps with a theme server: add `initialDataUpdatedAt: 0` to `useBrand`'s query (beside `initialData: cached`), or port the reference `useBrand`.
Copy the foundation files (`theme.ts`, `globals.css`, `tailwind.config.js`).
Regenerate `src/styles/tokens.css` (`scripts/tokens.mjs`): the derivation changed.

App code with `rounded-full` on buttons, tabs or pills: use `rounded-control` (circles keep `rounded-full`). Translucent `bg-*/70`-ish bars of the app's own: make them `/90`–`/95` with `backdrop-blur-md`.

Apps with a theme server: accept and return optional `infer`, `vibrancy` and `contrast` too, and fonts as keys with weights and tracking (see Fonts); accept and return an optional `fonts` (`{ headings?, body? }`, each `sans` / `mono` / `serif`); `useBrand`'s `withDefaults` takes a `SavedTheme`.

**Every app:** have the admin Brand & theme and Style guide pages with every theming feature (guide section 1, "Admin theming pages"); add them if missing, adapted to the app. Apps without a server: save the theme in the browser rather than having no Brand page.

Copy `globals.css` (the page background now reads `--bg-image` and friends; `.dot-*`). Apps with circles of their own: make them flat, side by side and at the guide's sizes (overlapping dots with rings, outlined or shaded circles, decorative orbs all go). Apps with a theme server: accept and return an optional `backdrop`.

Apps that track the reference: port the kit's `FullBleed`, `HeroSection` and `RangeField`, `AppShell`'s `width`, the Brand page's *Backdrop* section and *Share this look* section (export and import), categories, sub-tabs and search (`TemplateGrid`), and the *Type* section, the kit's radius and glass changes (`Badge`, `Tabs`, `PillTabs`, `ViewSwitch`, `Sheet`) and `AppShell` (top bar, dock).
Apps that track the reference kit: `divide-y divide-border` → `divide-etched` in `List`, `RankedList` and `Loading`, and the row padding change. App lists of their own: use `divide-etched` too.

releases.summary: Depth, glass and the circle motif; two colours are enough.

items.text: **Shades for every brand colour** (accent, highlight, support): `-lighter`, `-light`, `-dark`, `-darker`, a lit fill `-top` → `-bottom` (only ever moves away from the on-colour, so button text never gets harder to read) and washes `-950/900/800/700` for all three.
**Two-colour themes:** highlight is optional; `deriveHighlight` infers it from the accent, and support from both. `fullTheme`, `ownColours`, `OPTIONAL_KEYS`.

**Look:** `.glass`, `.card-glass`, `.orb-accent/highlight/support`, `.lit-accent/highlight/support`; lit `.btn-primary` with a glow; three colour orbs behind the page; cards at 90% so the orbs tint them.

**Circle motif:** `ThemeDots` (kit) before page eyebrows and in empty states; orbs by stat labels; lit-circle avatars; colour circles on theme tiles (inferred ones dashed); the starter favicon is three circles (recoloured from all three brand colours).
**Templates:** Canada (Flags) and Two-tone (Everyday, two colours).
Style guide: Shades and depth, Glass and orbs blocks; colours as circles.
`scripts/tokens.mjs` takes `-` for an inferred highlight or support.
**`Theme.highlight` is optional** (breaking for code that reads it from a `Theme`: use `fullTheme(theme).highlight` or `useBrand().colors`).
`useBrand()` returns `colors` (all four, inferred filled in) beside `theme` (as set); `withDefaults` keeps a saved theme's missing colours missing.
Brand page: *Infer it* / *Inferred* switch for highlight and support; saves only the colours that are set.

Kit: frosted `Tabs`, `ViewSwitch`, `Sheet`, `Pager` and top bar; lit active tabs, pills, select ticks and top-bar main button; `StatTile` and accent `LinkCard` glows; `Banner` without an image gets colour orbs.

**Lists aren't flat:** `DateBlock` is a calendar ticket with the month on a lit highlight band; row status dots are lit spheres with a glow (`STATUS_DOT`; `TONES[*].dot` now carries a shadow colour); `ListGroupLabel` is support text with an orb on a support wash.
`.card` is lit by the brand colours: a soft accent glow top left and support glow bottom right over its gradient.
Washes: `highlight-700` and `accent-800`/`support-800` added; `accent-hover` is now 20% (was 22%).
Sweden (amber highlight, sky support), USA (sky highlight, white support) and Hanukkah (silver-blue highlight): no white highlights.

appsMust: Copy the foundation files (`theme.ts`, `themes.ts`, `globals.css`, `tailwind.config.js`).
Regenerate `src/styles/tokens.css` (`scripts/tokens.mjs`): many new tokens.
Where app code reads `.highlight` (or `.support`) from a `Theme`, read it from `fullTheme(theme)` or `useBrand().colors` instead; the typecheck finds them.
Apps with a theme server: accept a missing `highlight` (as for `support`) and store only what's sent.

Apps that track the reference: port `useBrand`, the Brand page, Style guide, kit (`ThemeDots`, `DateBlock`, `ListGroupLabel`, `EventRow`, `TONES`, `STATUS_DOT`, `StatTile`, `Tabs`, `Sheet`, `Pager`, `EntityRow`, `EmptyState`, `Banner`, `LinkCard`, `ViewSwitch`, `PillTabs`) and `AppShell` changes. App rows built on their own date blocks or dots: follow the ticket and glowing-dot pattern (guide sections 2 and 9).
Optional: replace `public/favicon.svg` with the starter's circles (keep its four marker colours) so the favicon follows all the brand colours.

releases.summary: Up to four colours, flag and holiday templates, and apps hear about new releases.

items.text: **Support colour** — an optional fourth colour (`Theme.support`) for page eyebrows, avatars, third place and the page's bottom-left glow, with tokens `support`, `support-hover`, `on-support` and `support-950/900/700`. Themes without one get it derived (`deriveSupport`, `fullTheme`), so three-colour themes and saved settings keep working. `THEME_KEYS`, `FullTheme`.
**Flags** (10) and **Holidays** (12) template sets beside **Everyday** (`TEMPLATE_SETS`; `TEMPLATE_GROUPS` still lists every group; `sameTheme`).

**Version check:** the plugin runs `hooks/check-version.mjs` at session start; in an app whose `jimbo-ui.json` is behind the installed release, it says so and lists what's new. The skill states its version and does the same check when used. `scripts/versions.mjs` keeps every stated version in step.
Every Everyday template has a support colour; vibes name all three.
`scripts/contrast.mjs` also checks accent, highlight and support contrast, button text, and that the three colours are clearly apart (ΔE ≥ 20).
`scripts/tokens.mjs` takes an optional fourth argument (support).

Reference: Brand page has set tabs, four colour tabs and a support warning; `ThemeCard` shows support; `PageHeader` eyebrows, `EntityRow` initials and `RankedList` third place use support; `StatTile`, `Banner` and `Hero` take `"support"`; Style guide shows the four colours and support tokens; `useBrand`'s `withDefaults` keeps a saved support.
Starter default theme has a support colour (`#2EC5FF`).

appsMust: Copy the foundation files (`theme.ts`, `themes.ts`, `globals.css`, `tailwind.config.js`).

Regenerate `src/styles/tokens.css` (the support tokens are new): add a `support` to `BRAND.defaultTheme` if you want to choose it, then `node scripts/tokens.mjs <accent> <highlight> <background> [support]`.
Apps that track the reference: port the Brand page, Style guide, `useBrand` and kit changes above.
Apps with a theme server: accept and return an optional `support` (`#RRGGBB`) alongside the other three.

releases.summary: Branded **jimbo.ui** (the repo and plugin keep the name `jimbo-ui`).

items.text: **No logo — header text.** The reference `Wordmark` is replaced by `HeaderTitle`: the app's name (`BRAND.name`) in the display face and text colour, with any dot in the accent ("jimbo.ui"). The top bar, Style guide and Brand page miniatures use it.
**Starter `brand.config.ts`:** `logo` is gone; `name` is the header text.
**Brand page:** the uploads section is favicon-only.
**Server contract:** `GET /public/theme` returns `{ theme, faviconUrl }`; only `favicon` uploads (`/admin/theme/favicon`).
Showcase branded jimbo.ui.
`reference/web/src/components/Wordmark.tsx` and logo uploads.

appsMust: Copy the foundation files (comment changes only in `theme.ts`).

Apps that track the reference shell or Brand page: use `HeaderTitle` in the top bar instead of a logo, drop the logo upload row and `logoUrl`, and remove `logo` from `brand.config.ts`. Apps that keep their own logo can skip this.

releases.summary: jimbo-ui is now fully generic: no app's code, names, artwork or sample content.

items.text: **Reference kit is neutral.** Statuses are fixed **tones** — `Tone` (`accent` · `yellow` · `purple` · `red` · `muted`), `TONES` and `Badge` — that an app maps its own statuses onto; `EventRow`'s `status` is `{ tone, label }`. `ViewSwitch({ options, current })` replaces the list/map switch. `Banner`/`Hero` glows and `StatTile` accents are named `accent` / `highlight`. `RankedList` counts default to "item". The kit no longer needs an app's types or format helpers (`dateParts` and `initials` are built in).
**`AppShell` is reusable:** pass `tabs` (`ShellTab[]`), top-bar `actions` (`TopBarButton`), optional `onRefresh`, and routes as children; `DockIcon` draws tab icons. The showcase uses it directly.

**`Wordmark` is typeset** from `BRAND.logo` (`{ word, line }`) in the display face — main word in the accent outlined in the text colour, second line in the highlight. An app with drawn lettering swaps in its own SVG.
**Starter:** `brand.config.ts` gains `logo`; neutral name, prefix and favicon mark.

**Generic colour classes:** `accent`, `accent-hover`, `accent-950/900/700`, `highlight`, `highlight-hover`, `highlight-950/900/800`. The old `accent-lime` / `accent-pink` / `lime-*` / `rose-*` names still work. Foundation CSS and components use the new names.
The default template is named **Volt** (same colours).
Showcase content is neutral (events, places).
App-specific reference files: share images, photo carousel, upload ring, the API theme route and its table. The guide now describes the server contract (endpoints and shapes) instead.

appsMust: Copy the foundation files (`theme.ts`, `themes.ts`, `globals.css`, `tailwind.config.js`, `button.tsx`, `ColorPicker.tsx`). Existing class names keep working; nothing else is required for apps that keep their own kit and shell.

Apps that track the reference kit or shell: port the renames above (`StatusBadge` → `Badge` with the app's status → tone map, `status` objects on `EventRow`, `ViewSwitch`, `accent`/`highlight` prop values) and add `logo` to `brand.config.ts` if using the reference `Wordmark`.

items.text: **Stronger contrast on every theme.** Cards, fields, borders and secondary text no longer use fixed percentages: the engine steps each one just far enough to meet a contrast target on that background (cards 1.16:1 against the page, borders 1.55:1 against cards, muted text 5:1, labels 3.8:1). Mid and light themes gain the most — on Denim, cards went from 1.11:1 to 1.16:1, borders from 1.30:1 to 1.55:1 and labels from 2.8:1 to 3.8:1. Body text is a touch brighter (`#FAF8F4` dark, `#111113` light).
**Card borders at full strength** (`.card` uses `border-border`, not `/60`).
**Concrete** template background deepened `#55585E` → `#45484D` so body text reaches 7:1.
**Sheets render into `<body>` through a portal** (reference kit), so a parent's `space-y` margin can no longer push the backdrop down and leave a strip of the page uncovered at the top.
`theme.ts` no longer needs Google Maps' type definitions: `mapStyles()` returns its own `MapStyle[]` (same shape), so apps without Maps typecheck.

**Showcase** (`showcase/`): a demo app built only from the release's code — Home, List (search, filters, select mode) and Detail demo pages, the real Style guide and Brand pages, the shell and dock — published as a private page each release.

**Preview an update**: a skill workflow that reports what updating an app would change (versions, look, foundation diffs, local edits at risk, apps-must steps, reference changes, default colours) without touching anything.
`scripts/contrast.mjs`: contrast report for every template; `--check` fails the release if any template misses a target.

appsMust: Copy the foundation files (`theme.ts`, `themes.ts`, `globals.css`).
Regenerate `src/styles/tokens.css` from `BRAND.defaultTheme` (`scripts/tokens.mjs`) — the derivation changed.
Port the `Sheet` portal change into the app's kit (`createPortal(…, document.body)` around the backdrop).
If the app passes `mapStyles()` to Google Maps, nothing changes; if it typed anything as `google.maps.MapTypeStyle[]` from it, use `MapStyle[]`.

releases.summary: First release.

items.text: **Theme engine** (`foundation/src/lib/theme.ts`): accent, highlight and background in; every colour token out as CSS variables; light backgrounds flip text dark; map style, map pins and favicon recolouring.
**25 templates** in Dark / Mid / Light groups (`foundation/src/lib/themes.ts`), all passing the readability checks; an app's own default is added when it isn't one of them.
**Foundation:** `globals.css` (page background, type scale, `.card`, `.btn`, `.field`, `.chip`…), `tailwind.config.js` tokens, `Button`, `ColorPicker`, `cn`, gestures.
**Starter:** `brand.config.ts` (name, default theme, storage prefix), `tokens.css` (generated by `scripts/tokens.mjs`), `favicon.svg`.
**Reference:** UI kit, app shell with the floating tab dock, Brand page, Style guide page, wordmark, brand hook, `index.html`.
**Guide** (`skills/jimbo-ui/guide.md`) and the **jimbo-ui skill** with workflows to start an app, update an app, and release changes.

appsMust: Adopting for the first time: follow "start a new app" in the skill, or — for an existing app — split its own values into `brand.config.ts` and `tokens.css`, copy the foundation, and add `jimbo-ui.json`.
